findings.detail: This sentence was added by 94b7a1380, the commit whose stated purpose was to quote the measured compile walls. It states the opposite of what its own figure shows: 11.798116 > 10. The contradiction is internal to the fragment, so a reader cannot resolve it from either paragraph, and the checker does not read prose compile claims.
findings.summary: The compile reading says the read program's 11.798116 s and 11.791027 s are "well under the 10 s target", but both exceed 10 s, and the recommendation at line 32 calls the 10 s target the compile requirement that the stencil fit meets and the read does not.

findings.detail: The fragment says "Of the eight variant reads, one admits a valid, qualified state" and "of the four oracle reads, two do"; patterns 1 and 2 at :173 and :177 expect "<count> of the <total> variant reads admits" and so never match, leaving only the "three of the twelve rows overall" claim guarded. Verified by mutation: rewriting those two claims to "six admit" and "three do" still prints CONSISTENT and exits 0, so the commit message's claim to require "any count claimed over the reads" to match the receipts holds for one of three.
findings.summary: The validity-tally guard fires on one of the three tally claims the delivered fragment makes, because two of its four patterns do not match the phrasing 678985cc7 wrote.

findings.detail: Verified by mutation: changing the limited-converged interp axis error from 3.626 to 9.999 and the limited-converged fd axis error from 0.046 to 0.999 both still print CONSISTENT and exit 0. The prior review's blocking finding was that fragment figures matched no receipt; leaving two numeric columns of the same table unguarded keeps that class of defect open, even though the delivered values do match.
findings.summary: The error-table check compares only the two validity cells, so neither the axis-error nor the boundary-flux-error column is ever reconciled with the receipts that hold axis_error_m and boundary_flux_error_relative.
